input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: PB has no usable convenience exit. 14.2.2 is gated on SFJ having paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, closes on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, carries a redacted notice period, and conditions the exit on paying SFJ 300% of Development Costs, so over a Term running to the last Approval Payment (14.1) PB cannot leave on notice at the preferred (30 days) or fallback (60-90 days) standard. That fails the fallback on material terms. The redline cures the preferred checklist in operative language: 14.2.2's gating sentence and the 300% exit payment sentence are replaced by "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any, for the period after the effective date of termination"; the now-orphaned "reduced by the amount previously paid by PB to SFJ pursuant to this Section 14.2.2" credit is conformed; and new 14.2.11 bars SFJ convenience termination during the Term. Section 11.1.1.4 continues to govern the Trial Data Package transfer and its consideration. SFJ's event-triggered exits (14.2.3, 14.2.6, 14.2.10) and their payment formulas are untouched and consistent with 14.2.11, and the Section 5.2.2.2 cross-reference to 14.2.10 remains intact.

proposal.summary: PB may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts and no exit payment; SFJ barred from convenience termination during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We converted 14.2.2 into a genuine convenience right: PB may terminate on thirty (30) days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of any amounts it has prepaid, and the 300% Development Cost exit payment (and its credit reference) is deleted, leaving Section 11.1.1.4 to govern the Trial Data Package transfer. We also added 14.2.11 barring SFJ from terminating for convenience during the Term. Our fallback is 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any, for the period after the effective date of termination.

ops.text: 14.2.11 No Termination for Convenience by SFJ. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
